classification.difficultyReason: Link algebraic intercept calculations to absolute-value V sketches, using symmetry to establish both branches and reversing the opening for the negative absolute value.

content.prompt: Sketch each graph, showing the $x$-intercept and $y$-intercept.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3x+9&=0\\x&=-3\\y\big|_{x=0}&=|9|\\y\big|_{x=0}&=9\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-3,0)$. Draw the upward V through $(0,9)$ and $(-6,9)$.

spec.description: Upward V with intercepts -3 and 9; dashed guides to (-6,9).

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x-8&=0\\x&=4\\y\big|_{x=0}&=-|-8|\\y\big|_{x=0}&=-8\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(4,0)$. Reflect the upward absolute-value graph in the $x$-axis; it passes through $(0,-8)$ and $(8,-8)$.

spec.description: Downward V with vertex (4,0), y-intercept -8 and guides to (8,-8).

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x+13&=0\\x&=-\frac{13}{4}\\y\big|_{x=0}&=|13|\\y\big|_{x=0}&=13\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\tfrac{13}{4},0)$. Draw the upward V through $(0,13)$ and $(-\tfrac{13}{2},13)$.
